findings.title: SEP-10 JWT audience is never checked, so tokens issued for other services authenticate here
Firebase middleware is wired without requiring a verified email or phone, so unverified claims authenticate sign requests
Firebase ID token verified without revocation or disabled-user check
Shared service signing key is injected into the sign route with no operation policy, so any operation set for an authorized account gets co-signed
Sign endpoint signs any operation set for an authorized caller with no allowlist or time bounds

findings.title: Signatures issued for transactions without timebounds stay valid indefinitely
SEP-10 middleware is wired with an issuer that may be empty, so any JWT signed by the configured key is accepted
Any single registered identity can delete the whole account registration, not only the account owner
Identity values are never validated or normalized at registration, so recovery identities can be unverifiable or never match
Account insert returns without rolling back its transaction, leaking a DB connection per duplicate registration
Signing seed is accepted as a CLI flag that lands in process listings and shell history
Database rows are not closed when a row scan fails, leaking connections
Failed database ping only logs a warning, so the server starts with no working database
SEP-10 JWT issuer check is skipped when no issuer is configured
Stellar signing secret in source
